concept: Red portrait at a waterfall overlook
creativeDirection: Night location photography: build a real rocky waterfall overlook at night, led by a recognisable cast portrait and anchored by a physically plausible landscape drawn from the strongest sleeves.
scene: A nighttime rocky overlook beside a tiered forest waterfall, with wet stone ledges dropping away into dark cascades and bare trees framing the background. In the near ground, the man from source 1 stands close to camera, his pose and direct portrait presence intact, while the landscape around him carries the other album motifs as real features of the place.

elements.element: the man from reference image 1, close to camera, long dark hair and bare shoulders, lit so his face keeps the sleeve’s stark red intensity
the location is a real tiered waterfall with rocky pools and dark forest edges
two distant glowing human-shaped lights standing side by side in a small clearing across the water among bare twisting trees
two large weathered metallic head sculptures facing each other on a far ridge beyond the waterfall
a large reddish-orange moth resting on a foreground rock near the camera
angular red and dark blue accents in the lighting and surface colour contrast
deep theatrical crimson in the shadows and curtain-like darkness behind the trees
dusty beige haze muted into the stone and spray tones

coverSummaries.description: A high-contrast close-up photographic portrait of one long-haired man fills the right side, tinted deep red, with bare shoulders visible against a white background cut by a large diagonal red shape.
coverSummaries.people: one man in a close-up portrait with long dark hair and bare shoulders

coverSummaries.description: A nighttime photograph shows two glowing human figures standing side by side on bright grass in the center of a dark grove, surrounded by leafless twisting trees fading into blackness.
coverSummaries.signatureMotif: two glowing figures in a dark forest
coverSummaries.people: two people standing side by side, overexposed by bright light in a forest clearing
coverSummaries.place: a dark wooded clearing at night with bare twisting trees arching around a patch of illuminated grass.

coverSummaries.description: A dark monochrome collage depicts a tiered waterfall cascading over rocks and pools in a forested setting, with faint inserted fragments including a hand with red-painted nails, a small stringed instrument, and a tiny suited figure at the lower right edge.
coverSummaries.people: one tiny man in a dark suit standing at the lower right edge
coverSummaries.place: a rocky forest waterfall with multiple cascades, shallow pools, and dense vegetation around the stone terraces.

coverSummaries.description: Two enormous metallic head sculptures face each other in a field, their open mouths aligned toward the center, with a blue sky, clouds, distant trees, and a small building on the horizon.
coverSummaries.place: an open grassy field under a bright sky with clouds, distant trees, and a small structure on the horizon.

coverSummaries.description: A painted western scene shows a cowboy in a hat riding a dark horse through pale dust or mist, with a faint white cow emerging in the background and sparse dry brush at the bottom.
coverSummaries.place: a dusty open plain with low scrub and haze, with no buildings visible and a pale sky blending into the background.

coverSummaries.description: A jagged collage combines helmeted figures in red outerwear, angular blocks of dark blue and red, fragments of machinery or vehicles, and a small running silhouette on a pale ground.
coverSummaries.signatureMotif: helmeted figure in red raising an arm

coverSummaries.description: A framed illustration on a yellow field shows many colorful butterflies and moths arranged across a pale background, centered on a large reddish-orange moth with eye-like markings on its wings.

A painted theatrical composition shows three male portrait cutouts against deep red stage curtains, with one head upside down in the center and decorative miniature house shapes attached to the clothing of the two upright figures.
coverSummaries.signatureMotif: three male portraits against red curtains

prompt: A nighttime photograph from a low angle on a rocky overlook beside a tiered forest waterfall, camera close and slightly below eye level, with the scene opening leftward into dark cascades and wet stone ledges. The primary subject is the man from reference image 1, placed off-centre in the near ground at three-quarter length or closer, keeping his recognisable close-up portrait qualities: long dark hair, bare shoulders, direct gaze, still pose, stark presence; light him cleanly so his face is properly readable and carries a strong red cast against the darker landscape without becoming abstract. Build the place from reference image 3 as a real multi-step waterfall with shallow rocky pools, dark stone terraces, and forest edges. Across the water, include the support from reference image 2 as two distant glowing human-shaped lights standing side by side in a small clearing on bright grass among bare twisting trees. On a far ridge beyond the falls, include the support from reference image 4 as two large weathered metallic head sculptures facing each other. In the foreground on a rock near camera, include the support from reference image 7 as one large reddish-orange moth resting naturally. Let reference image 6 contribute only angular red and dark blue colour tensions in the environment, reference image 8 only deep crimson theatrical darkness in the tree shadows, and reference image 5 only muted dusty beige tones in stone mist and spray. Photographic realism, clean night location photography, crisp detail, no text, no collage look. Use moonlight and carefully hidden floodlights to model the rocks and falls, with the cast face clearly lit and the supports readable on second look. Strong visual hierarchy, asymmetrical framing, no crowd, no extra people, no fog effects beyond natural waterfall spray. Palette of deep red, black, charcoal gray, silver, dark green, white, and orange; mood ominous, dramatic, and precise. Reference map for people (the album images are attached in this numbered order): reference image 1 shows one man in a close-up portrait with long dark hair and bare shoulders. Copy each of these faces directly from that numbered reference image - same face, bone structure, hair, expression, and styling - rather than drawing a new person from the description. Nobody from reference images 2, 3 appears in the picture: use those images only for colour, setting, and objects, and add no figures, faces, or silhouettes from them. Hard constraints (override any conflicting source material): Create a single cohesive 16:9 image, not a grid, contact sheet, row of covers, or collage of separate panels. Do not reproduce the album sleeves as framed thumbnails, posters, record covers, or pictures on a screen, monitor, or television. A sleeve's abstract graphics, shapes, patterns, and colours may be painted onto the walls, doors, floor, or objects of the place as part of its decoration, without any lettering. Show no sleeve's faces, heads, or figures as a picture, mural, display, sign, relief, or silhouette anywhere; transform the sleeves' non-text visual motifs into one original composition. Include no readable text or lettering of any kind: no words, letters, numbers, code, glyphs, captions, titles, logos, watermarks, labels, or signage. Feature only adults and avoid gore, wounds, body horror, medical or anatomical imagery, blank or milky eyes, nudity, sexual content, weapons, and hate symbols; reinterpret any sensitive source motif abstractly. When a source includes a person, closely match their visible appearance and likeness to the reference image, preserving recognisable facial features, hair, skin tone, clothing, and styling, and their apparent age: every person is shown as the adult they are on the sleeve, never younger, smoothed, or more boyish or girlish. Keep each reference person in the pose, expression, and gaze the sleeve shows, and keep every identifiable face sharp, lit, unobscured, and in focus: no motion blur, long-exposure smearing, steam, fog, shadow, crowding, or shallow depth of field over a reference person's face. Expose the image cleanly whatever the light: every person's face well lit and readable, shadows that hold detail, and clear colour, with no murky underexposure, crushed blacks, heavy film grain, digital noise, or dust-and-scratches texture. Add no incidental plants: no flowers, potted plants, planters, climbing vines, ivy, hanging foliage, hedges, lawns, flower beds, or greenery framing the edges or carpeting the floor, unless the description above explicitly asks for that plant as part of a source motif or the year treatment. Dress the scene with the materials of the place itself - stone, metal, concrete, wood, fabric, glass, water, equipment - rather than vegetation. Everyone in the picture is photographed in the same place, at the same moment, under the same light as the rest of the scene, in full colour and with the same lens and grain: do not carry over a sleeve's own backdrop, studio lighting, backlit flare, monochrome, colour cast, or print texture onto the person. Each person stands inside the scene at the scale of the space around them, never as an oversized cropped head or bust looming at the edge of the frame over a distant scene, and never washed in red, blue, or other coloured light. Depict each identifiable reference person only once in the entire composition; do not repeat or clone them as another figure, reflection, mirror portrait, poster, billboard, screen, photograph, painting, silhouette, or background face. The only exception is repetition visibly intrinsic to one source cover: keep that repetition within that single source motif and do not echo the person elsewhere. The only people anywhere in the image are the reference people named in the reference map, and of those only the ones whose faces are clearly visible in their reference. Add no one else: no extra band members, musicians, staff, bystanders, passers-by, crowd, audience, background or out-of-focus figures, and no hands, arms, legs, or shadows of unseen people. Never complete a person who is hidden, cropped, turned away, blurred, or only partly visible in a reference with an invented face or body - leave that person out entirely. Photograph the reference people from roughly eye level, at three-quarter length or closer, in the near or middle ground, so each of their faces is large, sharp, and clearly recognisable in the final frame: never from directly above, and never as small distant figures.
